<!-- GENERATED by scripts/gen-api-reference.ts from sdk/openapi.json. Do not edit — including in Studio; the next build replaces this file. -->

::api-operation{method="GET" path="/v1/businesses/{biz}/emails/suppressions"}
#docs
Returned WHOLE rather than paginated — the list is small by nature. Exposed because an invisible block is its own failure mode: "we stopped emailing this customer and nobody can say why" is a support call correct bounce handling does not excuse.

## Path parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `biz` | `string` | **yes** | Business id (biz_…) |

## Response

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `object` | `string` | The object type; always `list`. One of `list`. |
| `data` | `array of object` | The suppressed addresses. |
| `data.object` | `string` | The object type; always `email_suppression`. One of `email_suppression`. |
| `data.address` | `string` | The suppressed email address. |
| `data.reason` | `string` | Why the address was suppressed — a hard bounce or a complaint. |
| `data.detail` | `string` | What the provider said, kept so a lifted suppression can be justified. |
| `data.created_at` | `string · ISO-8601` | When the address was added to the suppression list (ISO-8601 UTC). |

## Status codes

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `200` | Success |
| `404` | No such business |

#request
```bash [Request]
curl "$TMBILLING_URL/v1/businesses/biz_XXXXXXXXXXXX01/emails/suppressions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TMBILLING_API_KEY"
```
